thread:
sarah (security): FYI we just got a DSAR asking for deletion of a guest account's historical embeddings and a signed proof of deletion. Caller also wants confirmation that KMS-wrapped snapshots were purged. Do we have a recommended flow?

jia (privacy eng): Can you paste the requester email + scope? is this full-account or scoped to a project? :thinking_face:

sarah (security): Requester says entire account id guest-3472 including embeddings stored in vector-store snapshots and s3 archival snapshots. They also asked for time-to-complete and a proof artifact.

matt (infra): If snapshots are encrypted with customer KMS, we need to rotate/decommission those keys or delete objects and invalidate snapshots. But deletion proof for S3/GCS can be an erasure manifest plus logs.

lisa (legal): We need a signed proof package with: what was deleted, when, who authorized, and cryptographic evidence (keystore IDs). No raw keys in package.

jia (privacy eng): Proposed steps: 1) freeze inbound writes for account 2) run targeted erasure on embeddings index (vector-store) 3) delete archival snapshots 4) run cross-region propagation check 5) generate proof manifest and audit logs bundle. Anyone see holes?

matt (infra): Sounds right. Implementation notes: for vector-store TTL doesn't cover old snapshots. Use erasure-runner job with safe mode. Example command we use: 
```
kubectl -n privacy run erasure-runner --image=redwood/erasure:prod -- 
  --account=guest-3472 --mode=targeted --confirm
```
Make sure the job records keystore-state and snapshot object IDs.

privacy-bot: Reminder — retention-exception check required. If account has an active legal hold flagged in the retention service, erase must be blocked and escalated to legal.

sarah (security): Good call. I checked retention-service -> no holds. We still need RBAC guardrails: only a scoped short-lived role should run this.

matt (infra): Let's create a temporary role dsar-eraser:scope=guest-3472 with duration 2h, require mfa and key-access log. We should also require keystore audit token. Will add a make target: `tools/iam/grant-temporary dsar-eraser --account guest-3472 --ttl 2h`

jia (privacy eng): For KMS confirmation: if customer-managed keys were used, deleting objects alone isn't enough to prove non-recoverability. If the key owner requests, we can produce KMS audit events showing Decrypt/DecryptFailed and key rotation activities. For our managed keys, we can include key-version metadata and confirm zero-knowledge deletion of key material per our KMS policy.

lisa (legal): Include a short cover letter stating what we can and cannot prove (we cannot provide raw key material). Also include timestamps and the unique IDs of deleted snapshots.

sarah (security): I'll draft the erasure job and proof manifest template. Who can help validate the manifest fields?

matt (infra): I can add the IAM role and hook up infra-bot to collect the logs and S3 object deletion receipts.

infra-bot: Scheduled: create-temp-role dsar-eraser for guest-3472 (expires in 2h). Job: erasure-runner queued.

jia (privacy eng): After job completes, we should run a small verification: query vector-store index for fingerprint hashes of the account -> expect no hits. Also snapshot-list should show deletions with delete markers.

sarah (security): Timeline for requester: estimate 4-6 hours assuming no holds. If cross-region re-syncs exist might be up to 24h. I'll reply to requester with preliminary timeline and ask for confirmation if they want certified proof bundle.

lisa (legal): Ok. If they request certified proof, route through legal review before sending.

sarah (security): Action items: 1) matt create dsar-eraser role + infra-bot receipts 2) jia run erasure-runner and verification 3) sara (typo-sarah) draft proof manifest template and share for review 4) lisa prepare cover letter template. I'll update this thread with the manifest once ready. :white_check_mark:

matt (infra): On it. I'll post the role ARN and logs link once ready.

privacy-bot: DSAR workflow: retention-check -> role-grant -> erasure -> verification -> proof-bundle -> legal review (if requested).

sarah (security): Thanks all. I'll ping product/security on any escalation.

matt (infra): quick question — do we need to rotate the keystore used by job after deletion to avoid any accidental future decrypts?

jia (privacy eng): Good idea. For managed keystores we rotate the wrapping key and record rotation event in manifest. For customer-managed KMS, include guidance that they must rotate/decommission keys themselves if they want unrecoverability proof.

lisa (legal): Marking this thread for retention in case legal needs it later.

sarah (security): Closing loop: I'll post the final proof bundle and time stamps in here once erasure completes. Thanks!
